claims.text: Accelerated coupled degradation is caused by wear-induced removal of a naturally formed protective oxide film at elevated temperature.
Removal of the protective oxide exposes fresh reactive surfaces that are more prone to corrosion.
Corrosion causes surface embrittlement that accelerates wear.
Mutual reinforcement between oxide removal and corrosion synergistically increases overall degradation.
The as-fabricated eutectic high-entropy alloy has an inherent multiphase microstructure.
The as-fabricated alloy naturally develops thin protective oxide films.
Mechanical removal of the protective oxide occurs repeatedly at phase boundaries and interfaces in the eutectic structure.
At elevated temperature, the applied wear force strips the protective oxide film from the alloy.
Fresh metal exposed by film removal rapidly undergoes corrosion.
Corrosion products compromise local surface integrity and increase susceptibility to wear.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature will produce greater total mass loss than the baseline.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature will produce a higher wear rate than the baseline.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature will produce a higher corrosion current density than the baseline.
At the proposed lower-temperature baseline, the protective oxide film remains largely intact.
The proposed mechanism is limited to a defined elevated temperature, wear load, sliding speed, and corrosive environment.
Variability in oxide-film stability and interphase interactions affects the magnitude of wear and corrosion degradation.

contradictions.description: The baseline is variably defined as isolated wear, isolated corrosion, or a lower-temperature test. A lower-temperature isolated test changes both coupling mode and temperature, so it is not a single matched control capable of attributing the response specifically to the proposed wear-corrosion feedback.

The prediction and falsification rule require comparisons of total loss, wear rate, and corrosion rate against 'the control,' but a control undergoing only wear cannot provide a directly comparable corrosion response, while a control undergoing only corrosion cannot provide a directly comparable wear response.
